content.text: In this branch we've added a Jenkins setup to run on the Stellar intel cluster. I'd like to learn from that and now create a Jenkins setup for the Perlmutter GPU nodes (see https://docs.nersc.gov/systems/perlmutter/running-jobs/). It'll use the perlmutter-gpu machine files (in machines/) to build, run the unit tests, which automatically runs the GPU unit, and runregression should run tests on a gpu.

I’ll inspect the existing Stellar Jenkins setup and the Perlmutter machine configuration, then pin down the scheduler and test-launch details needed for a complete implementation plan. I’m using the repository’s directory-structure guidance because this is a build/CI integration task.

content.text: The existing Stellar pipeline is a manual, trusted Jenkins job: it builds two GPU-capable checkouts, submits unit and regression payloads through Slurm, and compares a candidate against its PR-base baseline. Perlmutter’s GPU configuration already enables CUDA/NCCL, and `runregression` will automatically run GPU variants (serially) on a GPU build during `check`. NERSC requires both `--constraint=gpu` and an explicit GPU request; one GPU uses the `shared` QoS.

questions.question: Which Perlmutter allocation should this CI request for each Slurm test job?

options.label: 1 GPU shared (Recommended)
options.description: Use `shared`, one task, 32 CPUs, and one A100; sufficient because unit tests and GPU regression variants execute serially.

options.label: 4 GPUs regular
options.description: Reserve a full GPU node in `regular`; higher cost with no present runregression parallelism benefit.

options.label: 2 GPUs shared
options.description: Use `shared` with two GPUs; retains shared-QoS charging but adds capacity for future parallelization.

questions.question: Should the Perlmutter integration mirror Stellar’s manual trusted-job workflow?

options.label: Mirror Stellar (Recommended)
options.description: Separate trusted Jenkinsfile, PR/ref parameters, candidate-vs-base baseline, commit statuses, launcher, and operational README.

options.label: Existing controller only
options.description: Add only the Perlmutter pipeline/payloads for an already managed Jenkins controller; omit controller/launcher setup docs.

options.label: Multibranch CI
options.description: Integrate Perlmutter into the repository’s multibranch Jenkinsfile instead of a dedicated manual job.

content.text: I’ll carry forward a one-A100 shared-QoS request (`-C gpu`, `--gpus-per-task=1`, 32 CPUs) for both payloads. The GPU regression runner supports both C and Lua inputs; the Stellar CI intentionally selects only C regressions, so I need to lock the intended coverage for this new GPU lane.

questions.question: What should Perlmutter runregression cover in this initial GPU CI lane?

options.label: C regressions only (Recommended)
options.description: Mirror Stellar’s bounded Level-1 workflow; `check` still runs each GPU-capable C test on CPU and GPU and compares both to the CPU baseline.

options.label: C and Lua regressions
options.description: Exercise all configured regression inputs and their GPU variants; broader coverage with longer GPU queue/runtime cost.

options.label: GPU smoke subset
options.description: Run a named small set of GPU regressions; fastest but requires curating and maintaining the list.

content.text:
<proposed_plan>
# Perlmutter GPU Jenkins CI

## Summary

Create a dedicated, manually triggered Perlmutter GPU Jenkins lane that mirrors Stellar’s trusted PR/ref workflow. It will build CUDA/NCCL Gkeyll using the Perlmutter GPU machine configuration, run all unit tests on one shared A100 GPU, then run C regressions with automatic CPU-and-GPU comparisons.

## Key changes

- Add Perlmutter counterparts to the Stellar CI pipeline, Slurm unit payload, Slurm regression payload, launcher, and operational README under `ci/jenkins/`.
- Add `machines/module_load.perlmutter-gpu.sh` as the shared Perlmutter module/runtime environment; refactor the existing Perlmutter GPU configure and dependency scripts to source it, preserving their current module versions and configuration flags.
- Configure Slurm submissions with `--account=$PERLMUTTER_SLURM_ACCOUNT`, `--constraint=gpu`, `--qos=shared`, one node/task, 32 CPUs, and `--gpus-per-task=1`, matching NERSC’s one-GPU shared-QoS guidance. [NERSC running-jobs documentation](https://docs.nersc.gov/systems/perlmutter/running-jobs/)
- Require Jenkins global settings for CI root, node label, GitHub credential, NERSC account, and optional build/time/timeout overrides; default the node label to `perlmutter-gpu`.
- Preserve Stellar’s safe candidate/baseline checkout model, GitHub pending/final status publication, Slurm polling/cancellation, artifacts, timing summary, and workspace cleanup, but use a distinct `continuous-integration/jenkins/perlmutter-gpu` status context.
- Build and install candidate and baseline CUDA builds on the login node; run `make unit-run` inside the GPU allocation.
- Compile C regressions before allocation. In the GPU payload, create baseline outputs with `runregression ... --c-only --execute-only create` (CPU mode by design), then run candidate `check`. The GPU build makes `check` automatically rerun GPU-capable C tests with `-g`, compare them against the CPU baseline, and report GPU-specific failures.
- Document manual setup, shared filesystem requirements, Jenkins controller/agent setup, environment variables, baseline bootstrap, validation commands, job launch/follow workflow, and recovery behavior for Perlmutter.

## Test plan

- Shell syntax-check all new/edited scripts and inspect Jenkinsfile parity against Stellar’s checkout, status, cancellation, and artifact behavior.
- On Perlmutter, manually validate dependency build, configure, unit-test payload, and regression payload in a shared workspace before enabling Jenkins.
- Trigger a Jenkins ref build and verify: one GPU is visible in both Slurm jobs; CUDA unit tests run; regression database records GPU results; artifacts and GitHub status are published; aborting a build cancels its Slurm job.
- Confirm an intentionally failing GPU test produces a failed Jenkins build and preserves Slurm logs/results.

## Assumptions

- This is a Level-1, C-regression-only lane, matching Stellar’s bounded coverage.
- One shared A100 is sufficient because unit execution and `runregression` GPU variants are serial.
- The Jenkins controller and its workspaces reside on Perlmutter-accessible shared storage, and the configured NERSC project has GPU allocation access.
</proposed_plan>
I’m implementing the dedicated Perlmutter GPU lane now. I’ll reuse the Stellar pipeline’s safety and lifecycle behavior, while adapting the machine environment and Slurm request to one shared A100.

This Level-1 CUDA CI lane is manually triggered after SSH/MFA authentication.
It runs a trusted pipeline, rather than pipeline code from the candidate pull
request. The pipeline builds candidate and baseline CUDA/NCCL installations on
the login node, then submits the unit and C-regression phases to Perlmutter GPU
nodes.

For C regressions, the baseline \`create\` run deliberately forces CPU mode;
the candidate \`check\` run executes CPU and GPU variants for GPU-capable

for example:

the \`shared\` QoS by default. NERSC requires both the GPU constraint and an
explicit GPU request. The shared QoS is appropriate for one GPU. See
